topics.title: [DEMO][NEXUS] What is NEX-27: one syndrome or multiple subtypes?
topics.description: RQ-001. Evaluate whether the harmonized synthetic evidence supports a single-syndrome or subtype model.

topics.title: [DEMO][NEXUS] Is immune dysregulation a central shared mechanism?
topics.description: RQ-002. Distinguish evidence for a shared mechanism from evidence for partially overlapping subtypes.

topics.title: [DEMO][NEXUS] Is KX-17 causal, downstream, or only correlated?
topics.description: RQ-003. Preserve separation between association, mechanism and causality.

topics.title: [DEMO][NEXUS] Does harmonization resolve disagreement or erase real differences?
topics.description: RQ-004. Debate what should be standardized and what site-specific information must remain visible.

topics.title: [DEMO][NEXUS] What should count as confirmed across five sites?
topics.description: RQ-005. Define replication and confirmation without collapsing uncertainty.

arguments.content: The harmonized evidence supports a subtype model better than either a single undifferentiated syndrome or a pure classification-artifact explanation.
A shared immune signature remains visible after harmonization, so the subtype model should not be interpreted as five unrelated conditions.
The strongest claim should remain limited: harmonization changes the apparent disagreement, but it does not by itself establish a biological taxonomy.
Clinical differences that remain after harmonization should be preserved as possible signal rather than treated automatically as residual noise.
The shared immune pattern is compatible with a central mechanism, but the active preregistered replication is needed before increasing confidence.
A mechanism claim requires prespecified outcomes and replication; the current signal is stronger than a chance observation but weaker than a confirmed mechanism.
Molecular heterogeneity remains compatible with a shared downstream immune response, so genomic diversity does not settle the mechanism question.
The correct state is supported-but-open: the consortium should not promote a mechanism from plausible to confirmed while the main replication is active.
The intervention prediction failed under the tested synthetic conditions, weakening a strong causal version of HYP-003.
KX-17 remains measurable and associated in several sites, but batch sensitivity means historical effect sizes cannot be compared naively.
The external cohort preserves a smaller association while failing to reproduce the strongest original effect; this favors a marker interpretation over a simple causal story.
The current knowledge state should keep predictive usefulness separate from causal status.
Harmonization must preserve source variables and transformation history so analysts can still recover site-specific meaning.
A reversible mapping is safer than destructive normalization because later questions may depend on distinctions that seem irrelevant today.
Clinical differences should only be standardized when they reflect incompatible terminology or measurement, not when they represent real phenotype variation.
The harmonized protocol should be versioned and auditable; otherwise the consortium can no longer reconstruct which definition produced which conclusion.
A compatible direction is not enough for confirmation when effect magnitude changes materially across calibrated sites.
Confirmation should combine preregistration, declared compatible methods and independent analysis rather than rely on repeated significance alone.
Sensitivity to a single modeling choice must lower confidence even when the headline estimate is nominally reproduced.
Public communication should expose replication status directly because the word confirmed carries consequences outside the consortium.
